items.title: Why Doesn't It Fall?

question.text: How can something this tall survive strong movement?

choices.response: Rigid towers fight the ground. This one is meant to move a little.

choices.text: It can absorb and control movement
choices.response: Yes. It is built to sway and settle.
It is meant to stay standing.

items.reveal: Tokyo Skytree uses modern structural damping. A reinforced-concrete central column moves somewhat independently from the outer structure, helping reduce earthquake motion.

moreInfo.title: Named after a pillar
moreInfo.text: The designers named the concept in reference to the central pillar found in traditional five-story pagodas. That is a name for the idea, not a claim that ancient pagodas supplied this engineering solution.

items.notes: Do not say Skytree copies a pagoda. Keep default copy short; depth stays in moreInfo.
